The instant petition has been filed praying for a direction to the respondents to pass rehabilitation
and resettlement award in terms of Section 31 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency
in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: 2.  The petitioners claim that their land was acquired and an award was declared by the Competent Authority on 13.4.2022.
However, rehabilitation award in terms of Section 31 has not been made so far.
3. Sri Santosh Kumar Singh, Advocate, has entered appearance on behalf of NHAI.

He submits that in the past, the petitioners had approached this Court by filing Writ Petition No. 26278 of 2023,
Affinity Agro Farms Pvt Ltd And Another vs National Highway Authority Of India And ... on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141907340/
1 with the grievance that the compensation amount in terms of award was not being disbursed to them.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It transpired in the said case that a rival claim was set up by two other persons and therefore the petition was disposed of by an order dated 25.7.2023 directing the Competent Authority to deal with the matter in the light of the provisions contained in Section 3H(3)/3H(4) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
He submits that thereafter, the Competent Authority has sent a reference to the civil court in terms of Section 3H(4) of the Act and the reference is still pending.

He submits that unless the reference is decided, it is not certain whether the petitioners are at all entitled to any benefit under the provisions of the Act and therefore, at this stage, no direction as prayed for, can be issued.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners is not in a position to dispute about the filing of the previous writ petition and the order passed therein directing the Competent Authority to deal with the claim of the petitioners in terms of Section 3H(3)/3H(4) of the Act.

5. Since as per statement made by Sri Santosh Kumar Singh, Advocate, appearing for NHAI, the dispute relating to title between the petitioners and other persons, has already been referred to the civil court, therefore, at this stage, we do not consider it appropriate to issue any direction for passing any rehabilitation award in favour of the petitioners.
We leave it open to the petitioners to make such claim in case their entitlement to compensation is upheld by the civil court.
6. The petition stands disposed of accordingly.

(Kshitij Shailendra, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 10.5.2024 Jaideep/-
